_comment: The user's ruled divisions, by lecture key. Hand judgements, exactly as runs/criteria.json holds pass two's. Positions are percentages of the transcript's characters, matched within 1.0 point. 'wanted' is every boundary the division requires; 'dontCare' is a boundary the user set aside, scored neither way; anything else a run proposes is unwanted. report-division.py reads this and never guesses.

l3.note: Ruled three times. 2026-09-08: all four contested cuts rejected — 'all these cuts split topics' — those being 18.7, 54.0, 88.5, 92.5, and the division 17 sections. 2026-09-17: shown the division d9 actually produces, the user accepted the single 1,137-word section that runs from 27.5 to 41.4 — invasion, then metastasis and its routes, then the benign-versus-invasive contrast — so 31.3 and 36.1 move to dontCare. They are not wrong boundaries; they are ones the user is content to do without, and a version that makes them is neither credited nor penalised. 2026-09-19, from the cut-site ruling sheet: 18.7 (L3-03, the move to histology) changes from unwanted to dontCare; 64.9 (L3-10) confirmed wanted.

l4.note: Ruled in two parts. Twenty of these twenty-one boundaries were already in front of the user when lecture 4's five criteria were judged, on divisions the old hierv3 prompt produced — sixteen of them in all six of those divisions — and none was objected to; every boundary those divisions made is still here. The twenty-first, the 150-word recap at 81.4%, appeared for the first time under d7 and was ruled its own section on 2026-09-17. All three subtopic-level criteria hold in 11 of 11 d7 runs: preamble separated, UV its own subtopic, animal testing separate from the Ames test.

l5.note: Ruled from the seam-proof artifact. Seam D (71.3) was rejected twice and then accepted; 57.3 was rejected and then accepted. 40.9 is the single-worked-example cut, rejected. 2026-09-19, from the cut-site ruling sheet: 10.5 (L5-03) changes from dontCare to unwanted, so 10.5 and 10.6 — the same cut site — leave dontCare.
